terms.meaning: A small icon a website shows in browser tabs, used here as a company logo.
Capital expenditure, the money spent on building or buying physical assets.
A setting that narrows a list to matching items.
Combining many records into one summary per item, such as one entry per company.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the pieces it needs
sections.what: Brings in React helpers, the router link, icons, the portfolio helpers, the project link helper, shared display parts and the portfolio filter hook.
sections.why: Likely reason: the list and cards are built from these parts.

sections.name: CompaniesView (part 1)
sections.title: Company filters, role filter and card layout
sections.what: Reads the company and role filters, builds the list of companies in scope, and shows a count. It draws each company as a card, either in one ranked grid or in groups by role. Choosing a company shows only that one, and Show all companies clears it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the filters let someone narrow a long list to the company or role they care about.
sections.watch_out: When a company is selected, the list shows only that one company, so Show all companies is the only way back to the full list.

sections.name: CompaniesView (part 2)
sections.title: Company detail panel
sections.what: When a company is selected, shows its logo and name, a three-number summary (projects, capital spend, industries), a website link, links to the dataset and map views, and a list of its projects with each project's role and cost. When nothing is selected, shows a dashed placeholder asking the visitor to pick a company.
sections.why: Likely reason: the panel stays fixed beside the company list on large screens (the sticky classes), so the detail remains visible while the list scrolls.
sections.watch_out: Capital spend shows as n/r when no value is reported, and a project's role is matched to the company only by its id or name, so a missing id can hide the role.

summary: Lists the companies linked to the projects in view, with filters for one company or a role, and two ways to group them.
purpose: Lets someone find companies and see how many projects and how much capital spending each has.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the grouping options. The limit of 60 items per page suggests long lists are shown in parts.
how: 1. Builds a company summary from the projects. 2. Collects the roles for the role filter. 3. Applies the company selection and role filter. 4. Shows company cards either ranked or grouped by role, 60 at a time.
inputs: The list of projects, a function that gives display names for industries, and the filter state from the portfolio hook.
outputs: Company cards, a count of companies in scope, filter controls, and a Show more button.
risks: Company logos come from favicons of external websites. The footnote says a placeholder tile is shown when there is no recorded website or icon.
debug: If the list is empty, check the project data and the company summary function. If a filter seems stuck, check the company filter value. Companies without a role appear under Role not recorded in the grouped view.
